scope: Defensive analyst training and harmless validation, not an attack execution manual. Use owner-provisioned identities, inert files and approved lab endpoints. Never collect real credentials or private communications. No snapshot/reset dependency. Commands are reference text and are not executed by the app.
taxonomy: This curriculum preserves the user's 14 groups and topic names. It is not an exact current ATT&CK matrix or a sequence that every incident follows. The official Enterprise tactics page reviewed on 2026-10-09 lists 15 tactics, including Stealth and Defense Impairment rather than a single Defense Evasion group. No technique-ID equivalence is asserted.

labs.title: Bounded port discovery and defender correlation
labs.prerequisites: Nmap already installed, a written target/port allowlist, a non-fragile lab service and agreed source IP. Replace the reserved example. Start with one host; for an explicitly approved small range replace the single address with that exact range, never infer scope from routing. Connection attempts can affect fragile services.

commands.title: Ordinary TCP-connect scan of three approved ports
commands.code:
# Replace 192.0.2.10 with the approved lab address.
nmap -sT -Pn -n -p 22,80,443 --max-rate 5 --max-retries 1 --host-timeout 30s 192.0.2.10
commands.interpretation: -sT uses normal TCP connections; -Pn skips host discovery, not logging; -n avoids DNS lookups. The rate cap bounds load, not stealth. Open means a connection succeeded; closed/filtered/timeout do not prove product absence or a CVE. No exploit scripts are run.

steps: Record UTC start/end, source address, exact approved destinations and command. Stop if the service owner reports degradation.
Run once and preserve output. Compare open ports with the owner listener/ingress inventory and intended clients.
Defender: query firewall/flow/endpoint logs for the source, destination, ports and window. Check whether successful and denied attempts are recorded; determine whether an alert is actually intended.

If an unexpected port is reachable, record excessive exposure and ownership. Establish software identity/version separately through approved inventory; do not label the port scan a vulnerability test.
After approved exposure changes, repeat identical ports/vantage and verify required clients still work.
labs.expected: A documented reachable-service list and correlated connection evidence. No alert is not a failure if policy only requires collection. No response is inconclusive.
labs.limits: Tests TCP reachability on specified ports, not UDP, application authorization, exploits, stealth or complete host inventory.

labs.title: Benign interpreter execution and endpoint visibility
labs.prerequisites: Approved Windows bench session, an owner-confirmed logging policy and access to the relevant source/collector logs. Process-creation events and command-line fields exist only if the corresponding auditing is configured; do not silently enable it.

commands.title: Launch a print-only child interpreter
commands.interpretation: Runs a child process that only prints a unique marker. It does not change policy, download code, create a task or persist. Preserve marker/time without secrets.

commands.title: Read event metadata for the same window
commands.code:
# Run in the same shell so $start and $end are defined. Security log access may be denied.
Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='Security'; Id=4688; StartTime=$start.AddSeconds(-5); EndTime=$end.AddSeconds(5)} | Select-Object TimeCreated,Id,RecordId
Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational'; StartTime=$start.AddSeconds(-5); EndTime=$end.AddSeconds(5)} | Select-Object TimeCreated,Id,RecordId
commands.interpretation: Metadata listing identifies candidate events, not the marker or parent relationship. In the authorized event viewer/collector inspect the matching executable, principal and parent; command-line/PowerShell detail depends on policy. Do not export unrelated secret-bearing message bodies.

steps: Run the print-only action once and record marker, principal and UTC window.

Locate the exact child-process event in source logs or the owner EDR console. Retain event ID, parent/child identity and available marker evidence; do not count every event in the window as this action.
Find the same event in the collector using asset, time and event ID. Record ingestion delay and completeness.
If an approved detection is expected, record query/rule version, alert time and routing. Ordinary PowerShell use may not warrant an alert.

Missing source event: investigate audit policy/access/retention. Source present but collector absent: investigate forwarding. Collector present but intended alert absent: investigate query/rule. Repeat after repair.
labs.expected: A traceable harmless process event, or a precisely located visibility gap. An observed process is not automatically an intrusion.
labs.limits: Validates benign execution visibility only; not injection, proxy execution, evasion or malicious script coverage.

labs.title: Create inert fixtures and detect a provenance/integrity change
labs.prerequisites: PowerShell and permission to create a new directory in the user's temporary area. Only the newly generated directory is written. Fixture paths are not service/startup paths. Preserve the files until review, then remove only that named disposable directory through normal file management.

commands.title: Generate and compare known harmless content
commands.code:
$lab = Join-Path $env:TEMP ('assessment-training-' + [guid]::NewGuid().ToString())
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $lab -ErrorAction Stop | Out-Null
$good = Join-Path $lab 'approved.txt'
$changed = Join-Path $lab 'changed.txt'
Set-Content -LiteralPath $good -Value 'TRAINING ONLY: approved amount=10'
Set-Content -LiteralPath $changed -Value 'TRAINING ONLY: changed amount=11'
Get-FileHash -LiteralPath $good,$changed -Algorithm SHA256 | Select-Object Path,Hash
Get-Acl -LiteralPath $lab | Format-List Owner,AccessToString
$lab
commands.interpretation: Two deliberately different inert text files should have different hashes. This demonstrates content identity, not authenticity: the baseline must itself be trusted. ACL output is not a complete effective-access calculation.

steps: Run once, record the generated directory and designate approved.txt as the instructor baseline.
Compare hashes and contents in that directory only. Explain why familiar filenames or signatures alone cannot prove approval.
Defender: correlate any available file-create/integrity telemetry with this directory and window. File auditing is policy-dependent; lack of an alert is not evidence of malicious stealth.

For supply-chain/persistence/escalation topics, apply the same reasoning to provided manifests/ACL exports, not actual service binaries. Identify who can publish/write and which trusted consumer uses the artifact.
For data manipulation, independently reconcile the fictional amount values. This is not ransomware, disk wiping or compromise of a live artifact.
labs.expected: Different content yields different hashes; permission and publisher evidence must be assessed separately. A trusted hash baseline plus provenance can identify an unexpected change.
labs.limits: Only instructor-created text fixtures are written. No live application modification, persistence installation, privilege escalation or destructive testing.

labs.title: Test synthetic-account authorization, logout and containment
labs.prerequisites: Owner-provided lab application with synthetic users A/B, two synthetic objects and an explicitly approved role/action/object matrix. Obtain exact fixture URLs from the owner; do not guess object IDs or enumerate real users. A test administrator must perform any account suspension/revocation through the existing approved process.
steps: Open separate ordinary browser profiles for A, B and anonymous access. Sign in with supplied test credentials without saving them into training evidence.

Through the documented read-only UI or developer tools replay of the approved GET, check A reading A's fixture, B reading B's fixture, anonymous access and A reading the explicitly supplied B fixture. Keep normal method/body; do not probe unrelated routes.

For each cell record expected allow/deny, HTTP status, redacted result, request ID and server authorization event. A redirect or error status is not a deny if the body still contains protected fixture data.

Log A out normally, then use the owner's approved application test harness to repeat the protected GET with the original synthetic session retained only in test memory. A browser replay using an updated or empty cookie jar checks anonymous access, not old-session revocation. If you cannot preserve that test context, mark revocation untested. Record timing and documented revocation/expiry semantics; do not copy tokens or cookies into notes.

To validate containment, have the designated lab administrator revoke/suspend only the synthetic test identity through the approved workflow, then verify access actually stops using the same retained synthetic session context. An alert/ticket without denied access is not confirmed containment.
If a deny cell permits protected data, stop expansion, record the exact boundary failure, fix server authorization/session policy and repeat every allow and deny cell.
labs.expected: Authorized fixture reads work; documented unauthorized and revoked-session reads deny without protected data. Record any policy-defined propagation delay separately.
labs.limits: No credential theft, brute force, forged tokens, pass-the-hash, session hijacking or real data access. App-specific paths and provider semantics must come from the owner.

labs.title: Read-only cloud and container control-plane checks
labs.prerequisites: Existing approved AWS CLI/kubectl installation and owner-provided read-only identities. Use only your allowed account, region, cluster and namespace. Do not install tools, obtain credentials or create resources. AWS IAM permissions and Kubernetes RBAC are different controls.

commands.title: AWS caller and bounded instance metadata
commands.code:
# Replace training-readonly and us-east-1 with the approved profile/region.
aws sts get-caller-identity --profile training-readonly --no-cli-pager
aws ec2 describe-instances --profile training-readonly --region us-east-1 --max-items 20 --query 'Reservations[].Instances[].{Id:InstanceId,State:State.Name}' --no-cli-pager
commands.interpretation: Protect account/identity metadata. Twenty items is a bounded inventory sample, not complete region/account coverage. A permission error does not prove no instances exist. Some API events require appropriate audit configuration.

commands.title: Kubernetes context, permission and one namespace
commands.code:
# Check context before making requests; stop if it is not the approved lab cluster.
kubectl config current-context
# Run these only after confirming context and allowed namespace.
kubectl auth can-i get pods --namespace training
kubectl get pods --namespace training -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,PHASE:.status.phase
commands.interpretation: Permission review and pod metadata only. No exec, deployment, secrets, role changes or host mounts. Namespace output is not complete cluster inventory and RBAC permission alone does not prove admission or workload safety.

steps: Record the approved identity/context before querying; stop on unexpected context rather than switching credentials automatically.
Run only the allowed read commands and capture resource identifiers, result and UTC time without secret material.
Defender: locate corresponding control-plane requests with actor, resource/namespace, action and result in the owner's audit tools.
Review provided inert workload manifests for privileged mode, host mounts and excessive roles; do not deploy them.
If inventory or audit is unavailable, record that gap. Repair read-role or collection configuration via the owner process and repeat the same query.
labs.expected: Only scoped resources are visible and corresponding read requests can be audited where required. Permission denial is an observed boundary, not inventory absence.
labs.limits: No container breakout, cloud writes, unmonitored-region deployment or logging tampering. Commands are not executed against AWS or Kubernetes during app verification.

labs.title: Runnable offline telemetry-gap and policy-decision exercise
labs.prerequisites: PowerShell, the bundled assessment/training_fixtures.json file and no target connectivity. Run from the assessment folder. These are fictional records, not Windows events or a live SIEM adapter; no fixture is automatically submitted to any collector.

commands.title: Classify source, ingestion, alert and containment gaps
commands.interpretation: Cases A-H independently exercise different outcomes. This simple priority classifier finds the first failed milestone; inspect all fields for multiple gaps. It does not simulate malware or validate production detection coverage.

commands.title: Compare per-event and aggregate policy decisions on fictional bytes
commands.code:
# Offline arithmetic only; creates no connections or data transfers.
$events = Get-Content -LiteralPath '.\training_fixtures.json' -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
$case = $events | Where-Object case -eq 'H'
$total = ($case.transferBytes | Measure-Object -Sum).Sum
$largest = ($case.transferBytes | Measure-Object -Maximum).Maximum
[pscustomobject]@{TotalBytes=$total; LargestEventBytes=$largest; Threshold=$case.policyThresholdBytes; AggregateExceeds=($total -gt $case.policyThresholdBytes); SingleEventExceeds=($largest -gt $case.policyThresholdBytes)}
commands.interpretation: Independent expected result: total 2400, largest event 600, threshold 2000, AggregateExceeds=True, SingleEventExceeds=False. A rule using only individual event size would miss this fictional aggregate policy violation. This is a defender query lesson, not a transfer tool.

steps: Run the classifier and compare with the independent answer key: A=EXPECTED OBSERVATION, B=SOURCE GAP, C=INGESTION GAP, D=ALERT GAP, E=CONTAINMENT GAP, F=EXPECTED OBSERVATION, G=UNEXPECTED ALERT, H=ALERT GAP.
Explain why F is healthy without an alert: collection was expected, alerting was not. Explain why E is incomplete despite an alert: expected containment did not occur.

Inspect H's fictional transfer metadata: four 600-byte transfers total 2400 bytes versus a fictional 2000-byte policy threshold. This tests aggregation logic in a classroom, not how to evade a detector.

Defender: translate the relevant fields into your organization's isolated test-query schema with the owner, and test known expected outcomes. Fixture replay can validate parsing/rule logic but not live sensor capture.
Record failed milestone, owner, correction and repeat result. Never generate the real harmful behavior to obtain a matching event.
labs.expected: Eight deterministic verdicts match the answer key; users distinguish source, forwarding, rule and response defects from normal no-alert behavior.
labs.limits: Entirely offline synthetic exercise. Cannot prove resistance to credential theft, stealth, C2, data theft, ransomware or destructive attacks.

groups.title: Reconnaissance
groups.goal: Understand information visible before access, and distinguish public exposure from privileged owner inventory.

commands.title: DNS and bounded service observation
commands.code:
# Replace reserved placeholders with one approved domain/host. No IP-block scan.
Resolve-DnsName -Name 'lab.example' -Type A
Resolve-DnsName -Name 'lab.example' -Type MX
Test-NetConnection -ComputerName 'lab.example' -Port 443 -InformationLevel Detailed
commands.interpretation: DNS records and TCP reachability are leads, not proof of product, ownership, vulnerability or authorization. Run from each documented vantage; failure is inconclusive.

verify: Get an explicit asset/domain allowlist and distinguish public-source review, target connections and privileged inventory. Do not extend scope to vendors mentioned in records.
Record source URL or command, UTC time, resolver/vantage and freshness. Compare observed facts with owner architecture records; label inferred relationships.
For exposure findings, show the exact unnecessary public detail or reachable interface, its owner and why it matters. Redact personal information; an email address is not a credential.
fix: Remove unnecessary public infrastructure detail and outdated records; restrict management exposure while preserving required DNS and business publishing.
Define an information-release policy and a reporting route for suspicious inquiries. Obtain owner approval before changing public records.
retest: Repeat the same public lookups or approved connection after record propagation; compare from the same vantage.
Confirm required service discovery still works and private details no longer appear on the reviewed surfaces.
groups.detection: Correlate approved connection checks with DNS, edge and application telemetry. Passive public research may leave no logs in your environment; do not promise detection of it.
topics: Active Scanning
Connections reveal reachable attack surface, not automatically vulnerabilities.
Compare one approved host/port check with firewall and service logs; separate IPv4/IPv6.
Restrict unnecessary listeners and monitor unexpected connection patterns.
Make one ordinary TCP connection to an approved service and locate its event; do not scan arbitrary IP blocks.
Gather Victim Architecture Information
Architecture clues can expose operating systems, hardware and cloud dependencies.
Compare owner diagrams, deployed inventory and public banners; identify stale or proxy-generated clues.
Remove unnecessary version disclosure and keep supported asset inventories.
Annotate a synthetic architecture diagram with public versus owner-only facts.
Gather Victim Identity Information
Roles and public identifiers can help target people; identifiers are not proof of account access.
Review an approved synthetic employee directory and role publication policy, without collecting credentials.
Minimize public personal detail and separate privileged roles from public contact identities.
Use fictional names and addresses to classify unnecessary role disclosure.
Gather Victim Network Information
DNS and routing clues expose boundaries and dependencies.
Reconcile approved DNS records and owner route exports; do not infer all hosts from one resolver.
Remove stale DNS, document external dependencies and restrict internal zone disclosure.
Map an approved domain's ordinary records to a lab topology.
Gather Victim Org Information
Published suppliers and schedules can support targeted pretexts.
Review owner-approved public business pages and identify unnecessary operational detail.
Publish only needed business information and verify sensitive requests through trusted channels.
Review a fictional vendor announcement for information-release risks.
Phishing for Information
A deceptive request seeks confidential facts without necessarily seeking a password.
Inspect a synthetic message for claimed authority, requested data and independent verification options.
Require verified channels for sensitive disclosures and make reporting easy.
Run an instructor-led fictional request tabletop; do not deceive real employees or collect responses.
Search Open Technical Databases
Registration, certificate and public repository records can expose assets; ownership needs verification.
Review approved public records and owner-owned repository exports; redact any accidentally exposed secret.
Use secret scanning, current registration contacts and certificate inventory ownership.
Classify synthetic certificate and repository metadata; never validate a discovered secret by using it.
Search Open Websites/Domains
Public web content may disclose people, technologies and relationships.
Record source dates and separate employer statements from speculation or third-party claims.
Remove unnecessary sensitive publishing and establish takedown/reporting processes.
Review a fictional job posting and label facts versus inferred technology choices.

groups.title: Resource Development
groups.goal: Recognize infrastructure and capability preparation while using only organization-owned training resources.
verify: Create an instructor-owned inventory of approved lab domains, hosts, images, accounts, tools and their owners. No third-party compromise or procurement is part of this exercise.
Review registration, certificate, repository and cloud audit evidence already held by the organization. Attribute with corroborating facts, not a shared IP or provider alone.
For each resource, document intended use, identity, authorization, provenance, expiry and an abuse-report contact. Do not download or execute suspected malware.
fix: Require ownership and provenance review for tools/images and protect cloud/domain accounts with strong authentication and least privilege.
Restrict unauthorized hosting and follow provider abuse or incident processes for suspicious external resources; do not take them over.
retest: Verify approved resources retain named owners and lifecycle dates and unauthorized changes produce audit evidence.
Repeat the procurement/provenance review on an inert example and check reporting reaches the responsible team.
groups.detection: Track unapproved resource creation, suspicious domain/account changes and tool provenance. Preparation on unrelated external systems may not be observable locally.
topics: Acquire Infrastructure
Infrastructure gives an operation hosting, identities and connectivity.
Review approved cloud resource creation, billing ownership and domain registration changes.
Apply resource ownership, account security and procurement controls.
Inventory an existing lab host; do not purchase or compromise resources.
Compromise Accounts
Existing accounts can lend trusted identity to an operation.
Correlate sign-ins, factor changes and owner-confirmed unexpected sessions.
Use phishing-resistant MFA, session revocation and protected recovery channels.
Analyze a synthetic account-takeover timeline; no account takeover attempt.
Compromise Infrastructure
A hijacked third-party service can host attacker activity.
Review owner-provided integrity and administrator-change evidence.
Patch management services and protect privileged accounts and hosted artifacts.
Use a fictional provider incident report to identify reporting and containment owners.
Develop Capabilities
Tools may be legitimate, dual-use or malicious; provenance and behavior matter.
Review source ownership, build records, hashes and declared permissions without running unknown code.
Require reviewed builds and restrict dangerous tool distribution.
Review a harmless script that prints a fixed marker; no malware or exploit development.
Establish Accounts
New personas or service accounts can support later activity.
Inspect approved account-creation events and business justification.
Require identity verification and expiry for service and external accounts.
Classify fictional account requests as approved, rejected or unresolved.
Obtain Capabilities
Externally obtained software and signing material introduce trust risk.
Check approved supplier, artifact integrity and certificate ownership records.
Use vetted distribution and protect signing keys; quarantine untrusted artifacts.
Validate a known harmless training artifact's hash against an instructor manifest.
Stage Capabilities
Hosted artifacts may prepare delivery or remote control.
Review authorized storage publishing and outbound destination inventory.
Restrict public artifact publishing and unauthorized remote-control endpoints.
Review a static inert-file hosting configuration without staging malware or C2.

groups.title: Initial Access
groups.goal: Assess entry boundaries, identity controls, exposed applications and supplier trust without delivering harmful content.

commands.title: Inspect an approved web entry point
commands.code:
# Replace with an owner-approved lab URL. A HEAD request is not a vulnerability test.
curl --head --connect-timeout 5 --max-time 10 https://lab.example/
commands.interpretation: Capture status, TLS validation and request time. Headers can be incomplete or generated by a proxy. Do not disable certificate validation to make a check pass.

verify: List permitted entry points, identities, partner connections and supplier/update paths. Obtain synthetic accounts and expected allow/deny decisions.
For exposed software, use the CVE guide to reconcile deployed versions and configuration with vendor conditions. Do not infer RCE from a web response.

Exercise one ordinary authorized request and one explicitly approved synthetic deny case; correlate edge, application and identity evidence. No phishing delivery, malicious document or rogue hardware insertion.
fix: Patch exposed components, require strong identity checks and restrict administrative access and vendor connections.
Enforce trusted update provenance, device controls and independently verified communications.
retest: Repeat the same permitted and denied entry checks and confirm normal users still work.
Verify patch/configuration evidence across replicas, alternate routes and partner access paths.
groups.detection: Join gateway, endpoint, mail and identity events by asset, principal and UTC time. A successful login is not automatically authorized business activity.
topics: Drive-By Compromise
A visited page can expose browser or plugin defects.
Review browser versions, isolation policy and web/endpoint incident evidence.
Patch browsers, remove obsolete plugins and restrict untrusted active content.
Use an inert local page to verify browser event collection; no exploit page.
Exploit Public-Facing Application
An exposed application's flaws can break its trust boundary.
Establish exact running build, reachable interface and vendor-defined affected configuration.
Apply vendor fixes, reduce exposure and isolate service identities.
Follow the applicable CVE's defensive checks; no generic RCE payload.
External Remote Services
VPN or remote desktop is an identity and network boundary.
Review sign-ins, allowed groups, MFA and device policy.
Restrict remote access to approved identities/devices and revoke unused sessions.
Use a synthetic account to test one allowed and one policy-denied login.
Hardware Additions
New hardware can introduce unexpected interfaces or trust.
Inspect device inventories and approved hardware-change records.
Enforce device admission and physical access controls.
Compare a fictional new-device event with the approved inventory; no rogue device installation.
Phishing
A message may seek a click, execution or secret disclosure.
Review a synthetic message's origin, destination and request plus reporting evidence.
Use mail controls, strong authentication and a trusted verification/reporting channel.
Run a clearly labeled classroom example without malicious links, attachments or credential capture.
Replication Through Removable Media
Portable media can transfer untrusted executable content.
Review removable-device events, autorun policy and file provenance.
Restrict execution from removable media and manage device access.
Analyze an inert file-copy event from a permitted training device; do not build self-spreading content.
Supply Chain Compromise
A trusted supplier artifact may be modified before deployment.
Compare signed artifacts, build provenance, dependency records and deployed hashes.
Protect build/signing systems and require reviewed immutable artifacts.
Detect a changed hash in two instructor-provided harmless files.
Trusted Relationship
Partner trust can grant access beyond intended boundaries.
Review partner principals, routes, delegated roles and access expiry.
Use narrow partner permissions, segmentation and time-bound access.
Review a synthetic partner-access matrix and identify an excessive grant.
Valid Accounts
Correct credentials establish identity, not legitimacy of every action.
Correlate session, device, role and business authorization.
Use least privilege, strong MFA and session lifecycle controls.
Compare an approved synthetic sign-in with a policy-denied test identity.

groups.title: Execution
groups.goal: Trace what ran, under which identity, and through which control plane; distinguish normal administration from unauthorized execution.

commands.title: Read process and service metadata
commands.code:
# Authorized Windows read access. Does not launch or modify services.
Get-Process | Select-Object Id,ProcessName,StartTime
Get-CimInstance Win32_Service | Select-Object Name,State,StartName,PathName
commands.interpretation: Access errors mean visibility gaps; do not elevate automatically. Point-in-time inventory misses exited processes and does not establish process ancestry; use retained endpoint events.

verify: Identify the execution surface: interpreter, application, service, scheduler, cloud API or container control plane. Record required role and expected benign use.
For one owner-approved harmless action, retain actor, parent/process or API identity, start/end time, artifact hash and request correlation. Never execute unknown binaries.
Compare source events, central telemetry and expected detection. A process existing or a shell being installed does not prove malicious execution.
fix: Limit execution and deployment permissions, protect interpreter/script policies and use reviewed signed artifacts where supported.
Patch vulnerable client/server components and reduce service/container privileges.
retest: Repeat the same fixed-marker or read-only action and verify telemetry and permitted business operation.
Use policy review or approved negative fixtures to confirm denied execution paths remain denied.
groups.detection: Record process ancestry and identity or control-plane API actor, object and result. A benign marker exercises visibility only, not coverage of malicious variants.
topics: Cloud Administration Command
Cloud APIs can request privileged actions without an interactive shell.
Review API audit actor, role, request ID and resource change.
Restrict management roles and collect organization-wide audit events.
Read an existing resource's metadata with a supplied read-only identity.
Command and Scripting Interpreter
Shells and runtimes execute scripts for legitimate or harmful purposes.
Review process ancestry, script provenance and role without exporting secrets from command lines.
Limit script sources and privileges and retain supported interpreter telemetry.
Run a fixed print-only marker in an approved local shell and locate its event.
Container Administration Command
Cluster exec/admin APIs expose a separate execution boundary.
Inspect control-plane audit events and exec permission assignments.
Restrict exec and privileged management roles and audit requests.
Review an instructor-provided exec event rather than entering running workloads.
Deploy Container
Launching an image introduces code and permissions into a cluster.
Review image digest, admission result, creator and requested privileges.
Require approved registries, image provenance and restrictive admission policy.
Validate an inert pod manifest against policy without deployment.
Exploitation for Client Execution
A client parser flaw can turn opened content into execution.
Compare running client build with vendor advisories and crash evidence.
Patch clients, isolate risky formats and restrict unnecessary active content.
Run existing benign document regression tests, not exploit documents.
Inter-Process Communication
Processes share data through interfaces with their own trust checks.
Review endpoint ACLs, caller identities and application message validation.
Authenticate/authorize callers and validate message structures.
Trace one documented benign request in a developer-owned test fixture.
Native API
Low-level OS calls remain observable through suitable telemetry; they do not universally bypass monitoring.
Review developer traces and endpoint events with exact build and caller identity.
Use least privilege and supported application controls and endpoint instrumentation.
Analyze a provided harmless API trace without writing bypass code.
Scheduled Task/Job
A scheduler can run code now or later under a chosen identity.
Inspect task action, trigger, owner and creation/update audit.
Protect scheduler management and trusted task artifacts.
Review an existing approved print-only task's metadata without creating recurrence.
Serverless Execution
Functions execute through event and cloud identity boundaries.
Review deployed code digest, trigger, role and invocation audit.
Use least-privilege roles, approved triggers and signed deployment provenance.
Inspect a supplied harmless function invocation record; no cloud writes.
Software Deployment Tools
Central deployment systems have broad execution authority.
Review deployment actor, package provenance, target scope and approval.
Separate approval from deployment and constrain operator roles.
Review a fictional deployment to detect unauthorized target expansion.
System Services
Background services execute with configured identities and paths.
Review service path, account, artifact writers and change events.
Use narrow service privileges and protect executable/configuration paths.
Inspect one approved service and document trust boundaries without modifying it.
User Execution
A human action can authorize opening or running content.
Correlate file provenance, user action and resulting application/process event.
Use safe content handling, application controls and clear reporting channels.
Open an inert text fixture and review ordinary application telemetry; no deceptive executable.

groups.title: Persistence
groups.goal: Review mechanisms that survive sessions or restarts without installing persistent access or modifying firmware.

commands.title: Read Windows startup and scheduler metadata
commands.code:
# Authorized host; these commands enumerate, not create, persistence.
Get-CimInstance Win32_StartupCommand | Select-Object Name,Location,User
Get-ScheduledTask | Select-Object TaskName,TaskPath,State
commands.interpretation: These views are incomplete and may need additional permissions. Review actions, principals and trusted artifacts in approved owner exports; empty results do not rule out persistence.

verify: Compare account/session grants, startup, tasks, services, extensions and server components against an owner-approved baseline.
For unexpected items, record creator, action/target, effective permissions, artifact provenance and triggering conditions without activating them.
Verify legitimacy with the owner and retained audit history. For boot, hypervisor or firmware concerns use specialist supplier evidence; OS inventory alone cannot exclude them.
fix: After preserving required evidence, remove unauthorized grants/components through approved response procedures and rotate or revoke affected access.
Protect startup/service/task writers and trusted deployment paths; patch supported software and use vendor-supported boot integrity controls.
retest: Re-enumerate the same mechanism and verify baseline and effective permissions agree.
Confirm normal restart/session behavior using existing lab procedures; do not install a backdoor to prove removal.
groups.detection: Track creation and modification events for long-lived access and activation surfaces, including cloud grants. A baseline difference is an investigation lead, not automatic malware attribution.
topics: Account Manipulation
Changed grants, recovery options or factors can preserve access.
Review identity changes, issuer, new permissions and owner approval.
Protect factor enrollment and role changes; revoke unauthorized sessions.
Analyze a synthetic MFA enrollment audit event.
BITS Jobs
Background transfer jobs can outlive an interactive action.
Review job owner, destination and notify settings in approved job exports.
Restrict unapproved transfer destinations and monitor job changes.
Review an inert job record without creating a download or notification command.
Boot or Logon Autostart Execution
Startup artifacts execute at boot or user logon.
Compare autorun locations, artifact hashes and writers with the baseline.
Protect startup paths and enforce trusted artifact policy.
Inspect an approved startup entry; do not add an entry.
Boot or Logon Initialization Scripts
Initialization scripts inherit boot/logon authority.
Review script source, assigned policy and effective writers.
Protect script repositories and policy administration.
Trace a benign documented initialization script through policy records.
Browser Extensions
Extensions can retain powerful browser permissions.
Review extension ID, source, requested permissions and enterprise policy.
Allowlist needed extensions and remove unsupported excessive permissions.
Compare two fictional extension manifests; do not install a rogue add-on.
Compromise Client Software Binary
Modified installed code may execute under familiar application names.
Compare deployed hashes/signatures with vendor or managed deployment records.
Protect installation directories and validate update provenance.
Detect a modified inert file using an instructor hash manifest.
Create Account
New accounts can provide durable identity-based access.
Review account creation, owner, roles and expiry.
Require approval and monitor privileged and service account creation.
Classify a synthetic unauthorized-account audit entry; do not create hidden accounts.
Create or Modify System Process
A new or changed service can become a lasting execution point.
Inspect service creator, path, identity and artifact permissions.
Restrict service management and protect service binaries.
Review a fictional service-change event against a baseline.
Event Triggered Execution
A registered event consumer can activate code later.
Review subscription/trigger definitions, action target and owner.
Restrict event-consumer writers and audit registration changes.
Analyze a static event-subscription export without registering actions.
External Remote Services
Remote access can persist through grants and sessions.
Review remote access policy, session age and unused accounts.
Expire unused access and require strong device/identity checks.
Verify a synthetic revoked session cannot perform an approved protected read.
Hijack Execution Flow
Trusted code may load an unintended library or executable.
Review resolved paths, module provenance and directory write permissions.
Use explicit protected load paths and controlled dependencies.
Inspect a developer-provided module-load trace; do not plant a DLL.
Hypervisor
The VM management layer is a high-trust boundary, not automatically hidden from all sensors.
Review hypervisor patch level, admin audit and vendor integrity evidence.
Protect management access and maintain supported hypervisor builds.
Review a fictional manager integrity alert with the platform owner.
Office Application Startup
Templates and add-ins may activate on application launch.
Review approved add-in/template paths, signatures and policy.
Restrict trusted locations and unsigned or unnecessary add-ins.
Inspect an exported add-in inventory; no macro or template injection.
Pre-OS Boot
Firmware and boot components operate below ordinary applications.
Review vendor attestation, boot measurements and hardware management changes.
Use supported secure/measured boot and protected firmware update channels.
Interpret supplied boot-attestation records; no firmware modification.
Scheduled Task/Job
Recurring tasks can restore unwanted activity.
Review task trigger, action, identity, writers and creation history.
Protect task administration and alert on unauthorized recurrence.
Compare an approved task export with a fictional unapproved change.
Server Software Component
Plugins, handlers and server modules can retain application-level access.
Review deployment hashes, module inventory and change audit.
Limit server write privileges and use reviewed immutable deployments.
Compare server manifests; do not install a web shell.
Traffic Signaling
Network-triggered activity may be intermittent rather than continuously connected.
Correlate flow timing with service/process activation using provided telemetry.
Restrict inbound exposure and retain network/endpoint correlation.
Analyze a synthetic timing trace; do not implement hidden packet triggers.
Valid Accounts
Long-lived grants, keys or sessions can maintain account access.
Review session/token metadata, grant age, issuer and revocation evidence without token values.
Apply short-lived access, grant review and effective revocation.
Check a supplied synthetic identity's revocation evidence.

groups.title: Privilege Escalation
groups.goal: Establish lower-to-higher privilege trust failures through permission, configuration and patch evidence, not elevation payloads.

commands.title: Read current identity and an approved ACL
commands.code:
# Authorized session. Output contains identity metadata; protect it.
whoami /user
whoami /groups
Get-Acl -LiteralPath 'C:\ApprovedAssessment\service-config.example' | Format-List Owner,AccessToString
commands.interpretation: Replace the path with an approved artifact. Group membership and displayed ACLs are not a complete effective-access calculation. Do not execute or modify the service artifact.

verify: Name the starting principal, permitted actions and higher-privilege consumer. Separate administrator-only evidence from ordinary-user capability.
Review effective writers of privileged artifacts and directories, task/service identities, policy and vendor patch prerequisites.
Confirm each alleged trust failure using owner-approved permission evaluation or existing regression evidence; do not steal tokens, inject processes or trigger kernel exploits.
fix: Reduce excessive grants and protect artifacts consumed by privileged processes, including parent-directory rights.
Patch affected hosts/runtimes and enforce supported container/VM isolation and elevation policies.
retest: Re-evaluate effective access for the original lower-privilege role and verify it cannot control the privileged artifact.
Confirm expected service and user workflows still work and capture revised build/configuration evidence.
groups.detection: Correlate identity/group changes, privileged execution and artifact writes. A high-privilege service by itself is not an escalation finding.
topics: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism
Elevation controls enforce or prompt for a privilege boundary.
Review effective elevation policy, privileged rules and audit results.
Minimize elevation rights and patch supported control mechanisms.
Inspect policy and supplied allow/deny events without bypassing prompts.
Access Token Manipulation
Security tokens carry process identity and authorization context.
Review privileged identity transitions and relevant endpoint audit evidence.
Limit token-related privileges and protect privileged processes.
Analyze synthetic identity-transition records; no token stealing or duplication.
Boot or Logon Autostart Execution
Startup execution can inherit elevated authority.
Compare startup principal with artifact and directory writers.
Protect startup artifacts and avoid unnecessary privileged startup.
Review a fictional writable-startup finding using ACL evidence.
Boot or Logon Initialization Scripts
Privileged initialization trusts scripts and their publishers.
Review policy owner, execution role and script-store permissions.
Protect policy/script publishing and separate administrator duties.
Map a benign script's writers and execution identity.
Create or Modify System Process
Service configuration can cross a privilege boundary.
Inspect service management rights and effective executable/configuration writers.
Restrict service changes and use least-privilege identities.
Evaluate a provided service ACL without changing it.
Escape to Host
Host escape crosses container or virtual-machine isolation.
Review runtime patches, privileged flags, host mounts and isolation configuration.
Patch isolation layers and remove unnecessary host privileges/mounts.
Assess an inert container manifest; no breakout attempt.
Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
A local vulnerability may elevate a starting identity under specific conditions.
Check exact running OS/component build, prerequisites and vendor servicing records.
Apply vendor fixes and reduce local attack surface.
Use the CVE's applicability procedure; do not execute a kernel exploit.
Hijack Execution Flow
A privileged consumer may trust code from a writable location.
Establish actual module resolution and lower-privilege write authority.
Use protected explicit load paths and verified artifacts.
Review a supplied module trace and ACL pair; do not plant code.
Process Injection
One process may tamper with another process's execution context.
Review cross-process access and endpoint alerts with principal/process provenance.
Restrict unnecessary debugging rights and maintain endpoint protections.
Analyze prerecorded synthetic cross-process events without opening privileged process memory.
Scheduled Task/Job
Privileged tasks may trust mutable actions or configuration.
Review task principal and writers of its definition, script and parent directories.
Protect task management and trusted action paths.
Assess an instructor-provided task export for excessive writers.
Valid Accounts
An already privileged account provides high authority without a software exploit.
Review role assignments, justification and sign-in/session provenance.
Use just-in-time privilege and strong authentication for administrator roles.
Compare fictional administrator grants with an approved role matrix.

groups.title: Defense Evasion
groups.goal: Find visibility, integrity and control gaps using harmless fixtures and evidence review, without teaching concealment or disabling defenses.

commands.title: Read security posture and recent event metadata
commands.code:
# Read-only Windows inspection; available features and privileges vary.
Get-NetFirewallProfile | Select-Object Name,Enabled
Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='System'; StartTime=(Get-Date).AddHours(-1)} -MaxEvents 20 | Select-Object TimeCreated,Id,ProviderName
commands.interpretation: Local state/events do not prove central visibility or enforcement. Access errors and missing events need diagnosis. Do not change firewall, logging or security-agent settings.

verify: Define the expected sensor and integrity source for each surface, including cloud regions, control-plane changes, endpoint processes and boot components.

Use a supplied inert event/trace to test a query, or perform a normal authorized action with a fixed marker. Record whether this validates source collection, ingestion, rule matching or response; replay is not live attack validation.
Compare approved security posture and trusted inventories with retained change history. Missing telemetry is a gap, not proof of successful stealth or absence of activity.
fix: Repair collection health, restrict changes to security controls and protect logs and trusted software paths.
Use vendor-supported application, identity, boot and endpoint controls. Validate signed code provenance; signatures alone do not guarantee benign behavior.
retest: Repeat the identical harmless event or posture review and verify source-to-collector completeness and intended alert routing.
Confirm legitimate actions still work. Record coverage limits instead of claiming all evasion variants are detected.
groups.detection: Distinguish source absence, forwarding loss, retention loss, query error and missed alert. Track security-control tampering with an independent telemetry source; never demonstrate by disabling defenses.
topics: Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism
Unexpected elevated execution can bypass intended approval.
Review policy and elevation outcomes with requester identity.
Restrict elevation and collect independent approval/audit evidence.
Analyze an inert unexpected-elevation event; no bypass.
Access Token Manipulation
Changed security context can obscure which identity acted.
Correlate process identity transitions with sign-in and privilege records.
Limit sensitive token privileges and protect privileged sessions.
Review synthetic identity-transition evidence; no impersonation.
ASLR/DEP Bypass
Memory protections complicate exploitation but do not eliminate bugs.
Review supported mitigation configuration and compiler/runtime evidence.
Patch defects and enable compatible current mitigations.
Interpret a developer-provided mitigation report; no bypass construction.
Build Image on Host
Local builds can introduce unreviewed artifacts outside deployment controls.
Review build-tool activity, source ownership and resulting artifact provenance.
Require reviewed build/deployment paths and least-privilege build identities.
Review a harmless build manifest and its hash inventory.
Clear Windows Event Logs / Linux History
Evidence removal can break investigations; shell history is not a reliable primary audit source.
Review log continuity, retention and independently collected audit events.
Protect central logs and restrict local log administration.
Replay a synthetic log-clear event into an isolated query test; do not clear logs.
Debugger Evasion
Software may change behavior under analysis, creating observation bias.
Review provided behavioral reports across documented environments.
Use corroborating telemetry and qualified analysis procedures.
Compare two fictional analysis reports; no anti-analysis code.
Deobfuscate/Decode Files or Information
Decoded content can differ from its stored representation.
Review approved static artifact metadata and process ancestry without decoding unknown payloads.
Apply behavioral controls and quarantine untrusted artifacts.
Compare a known harmless text fixture's representations, not executable content.
Deploy Container
Short-lived workloads can disappear before inventory polling.
Use retained create/delete and admission audit with image digest.
Require registry/provenance policy and durable control-plane telemetry.
Analyze synthetic container lifecycle events without deployment.
Direct Volume Access
Raw device access may bypass ordinary file-level observation.
Review device-access permissions and retained endpoint storage events.
Restrict raw device privileges and protect storage integrity.
Inspect permission evidence; never read raw sectors.
Execution Guardrails
Conditional execution can make one test environment unrepresentative.
Review provided static conditions and environment assumptions.
Use corroborating source, configuration and behavioral evidence.
Identify scope limits in a fictional conditional-execution report.
Exploitation for Defense Evasion
A security component's defect may undermine enforcement.
Match exact product build and vendor advisory prerequisites.
Patch supported security tooling and monitor its health independently.
Review vendor-fixed build evidence; no attack on antivirus/EDR.
File and Directory Permissions Modification
Changed ACLs may prevent sensors or analysts reading artifacts.
Compare effective permissions and actor/change history with the baseline.
Restrict ACL changes and monitor protected locations.
Analyze an instructor-provided ACL diff without modifying permissions.
Hide Artifacts
Unexpected storage locations or attributes can obscure inventory.
Review owner-provided file metadata, inventory coverage and changes.
Use trusted inventories and monitor protected artifact changes.
Find an inert unexpected entry in a static file manifest.
Hijack Execution Flow
Trusted programs may resolve untrusted code paths.
Correlate module provenance, resolved paths and writer rights.
Use protected load paths and verified deployment artifacts.
Inspect a module-load trace without planting a library.
Impair Defenses
Disabled controls or broken pipelines reduce defensive capability.
Check independent agent heartbeat, policy and control-change audit.
Protect control management and alert on health/policy drift.
Use a synthetic missing-heartbeat fixture; do not stop agents or firewalls.
Indicator Removal
Deleted artifacts can leave only indirect retained evidence.
Correlate file/change timelines with independently retained events.
Protect audit retention and preserve incident evidence before cleanup.
Reconstruct a fictional deletion timeline; do not erase artifacts.
Masquerading
A familiar name can conceal an unfamiliar artifact.
Compare path, signature, hash, parent and publisher rather than name alone.
Apply trusted artifact policy and monitor provenance mismatches.
Distinguish two inert manifests with the same filename but different provenance.
Modify Authentication Process
Changed identity components can alter trust decisions.
Review provider/library integrity, configuration and administrator audit.
Protect identity deployment and require independent change approval.
Review a fictional authentication configuration diff; no tampering.
Modify Cloud Compute Infrastructure
Control-plane changes can alter logging or security boundaries.
Review organization audit, effective policy and change actor across regions.
Restrict security-policy changes and collect independent audit evidence.
Classify a synthetic cloud-policy-change event without cloud writes.
Modify System Image
An altered base or recovery image can propagate compromised state.
Compare approved image digests and build provenance.
Protect image publishing and enforce immutable reviewed builds.
Identify a mismatched inert image manifest.
Network Boundary Flyby
Unexpected protocol paths can violate intended boundary policy.
Review actual application/protocol identity and allowed flows, not just ports.
Use explicit egress/ingress policy and application-aware monitoring.
Analyze a synthetic unexpected protocol/port event; no bypass traffic.
Obfuscated Files or Information
Encoding or packing alone does not establish malicious intent.
Review provenance and behavioral evidence rather than entropy alone.
Use layered artifact/behavior controls and safe quarantine.
Classify a harmless encoded text sample without executing decoded content.
Plc/Firmware Modification
Device firmware changes can affect both visibility and physical safety.
Review supplier integrity, firmware revision and maintenance records with the OT owner.
Restrict firmware updates and use vendor-supported signed releases.
Conduct an OT-owner tabletop; no device modification or live probing.
Pre-OS Boot
Boot-layer compromise cannot be excluded by a process list.
Review boot attestation and supplier-supported integrity evidence.
Protect boot configuration and firmware update channels.
Interpret prerecorded attestation results without firmware writes.
Process Injection
Cross-process tampering can separate executing code from its origin.
Correlate cross-process access alerts with identities and artifact provenance.
Limit debug rights and retain endpoint behavioral telemetry.
Analyze synthetic events; no process injection.
Rootkit
Low-level tampering can make one host's reports unreliable.
Compare independent boot, endpoint, network and trusted integrity evidence.
Use supported hardening and specialist incident handling.
Analyze conflicting fictional reports; no kernel modification.
Subvert Trust Controls
A valid signature can be misused or belong to a compromised signer.
Review signer ownership, artifact provenance and revocation status.
Protect signing keys and enforce supplier/build trust policy.
Review synthetic signer/provenance mismatches; no stolen certificates.
System Binary Proxy Execution
Trusted utilities can still perform unauthorized actions.
Review parent, arguments, target provenance and resulting behavior, with secrets redacted.
Constrain unnecessary utility use and rely on behavioral context.
Analyze a supplied inert utility event; no proxy payload execution.
Traffic Signaling
Intermittent activation can escape continuous-connection assumptions.
Correlate provided network timing with endpoint activation events.
Retain network/host correlation and restrict unnecessary reachability.
Review a synthetic timing fixture; no covert trigger implementation.
Trusted Developer Utilities Proxy Execution
Build utilities have legitimate code-execution authority.
Review project provenance, caller role and process ancestry.
Constrain build environments and require reviewed projects/artifacts.
Inspect a harmless project manifest; no utility-based payload.
Unused/Unsupported Cloud Regions
Regions outside monitoring coverage can hold unreviewed resources.
Compare region resource inventory with organization-wide collection coverage.
Apply supported region policies and comprehensive audit collection.
Find a gap in a fictional region inventory; no resource creation.
Use Alternate Authentication Material
Tokens and sessions may authorize actions without a password prompt.
Review issuer, scope, expiry and revocation metadata without token values.
Protect short-lived grants and validate issuer/audience and revocation.
Analyze synthetic token metadata; no replay of stolen material.
Valid Accounts
Legitimate identities can perform unauthorized business actions.
Correlate account, device, role, resource and approved intent.
Use least privilege and risk-aware session controls.
Compare allowed and denied synthetic access cases without compromising accounts.
Virtualization/Sandbox Evasion
Environment-dependent behavior limits conclusions from one analysis run.
Review stated test conditions and independent evidence sources.
Use qualified analysis and explicitly document observation limits.
Compare fictional environment reports; no sandbox-detection or evasion code.

groups.title: Credential Access
groups.goal: Protect authentication material and recognize exposure evidence without collecting, cracking or replaying real secrets.
verify: Inventory credential-bearing stores and identity flows from approved architecture and policy exports; record metadata, not secret values.
Review access controls, secret lifetime, transport protection, token validation and retained identity events. Discovery of a suspected secret is an incident-handling matter; do not test it by login.
Use synthetic identities and instructor-provided redacted fixtures to check expected deny/revoke decisions. No password spraying, keylogging, ticket cracking or memory dumping.
fix: Apply phishing-resistant authentication, least privilege, protected secret stores and short-lived tightly scoped tokens where supported.
If exposure is established, preserve evidence and revoke/rotate affected secrets through the owner's incident process; patch underlying defects.
retest: Verify access and revocation policy with a supplied synthetic identity, without copying raw tokens into evidence.
Review updated secret-scanning, access and authentication audit evidence and confirm legitimate access remains possible.
groups.detection: Correlate unusual access to credential stores, factor/grant changes and sign-in anomalies with identity context. Never include passwords, hashes, keys, raw cookies or tokens in training records.
topics: Adversary-in-the-Middle
An intermediary can observe or alter traffic when peer trust is weak.
Review TLS/peer validation, network trust and owner-provided negotiation logs.
Require validated encrypted transport and phishing-resistant authentication.
Interpret a synthetic certificate-validation failure; no interception.
Brute Force
Repeated authentication attempts may guess passwords or spray identities.
Review aggregate failure/lockout events, rate limits and principal context.
Use strong MFA, rate limiting and protected recovery workflows.
Evaluate a prerecorded synthetic failure series; do not guess passwords.
Credentials from Password Stores
Secret stores require careful access and process boundaries.
Review store policy and access telemetry without opening saved passwords.
Protect stores, endpoints and browser policies with least privilege.
Analyze an inert unexpected-store-access alert; no extraction.
Exploitation for Credential Access
A flaw can expose secret-bearing memory or storage.
Match running component build and vendor-defined prerequisites.
Patch the component and revoke exposed material if evidence supports exposure.
Use vendor applicability evidence; no credential dumping.
Forge Web Credentials
Broken token validation can accept untrusted assertions.
Review issuer, audience, signature/key trust and documented negative regression tests.
Use supported identity libraries and strict validation with trusted keys.
Review developer-provided invalid-token test results; no forged login tokens.
Input Capture
Captured input may disclose secrets before secure transport helps.
Review approved endpoint/UI integrity and access to input-capture functions.
Restrict untrusted software and protect authentication UI.
Analyze a fictional capture alert; no keylogger or fake prompt.
Kerberoasting / AS-REP Roasting
Some directory account settings and ticket exposure create offline guessing risk.
Review service-account configuration, encryption policy and preauthentication exceptions with the directory owner.
Use managed service accounts, strong unique secrets and required preauthentication.
Review a synthetic account-policy export; no ticket harvesting or cracking.
Network Sniffing
Packet visibility can expose cleartext data when network/transport controls fail.
Review sensor authorization, negotiated protection and collection policy.
Use encrypted protocols and restrict capture privileges.
Inspect metadata from a supplied synthetic packet fixture; no live credential capture.
OS Credential Dumping
Core identity memory and databases are sensitive boundaries.
Review protection policy and unexpected access alerts without reading memory or password databases.
Protect privileged processes and restrict debugging/admin rights.
Analyze an instructor-provided access alert; do not access LSASS or shadow secrets.
Phishing for Credentials
Deceptive login requests can harvest secrets or approve unwanted access.
Review fictional message/domain evidence and trusted reporting paths.
Use phishing-resistant MFA and independent request verification.
Run a labeled classroom example without a functioning credential form.
Steal Application Access Tokens
OAuth grants can authorize service access independently of passwords.
Review consent, scope, issuer, device and revocation metadata.
Limit consent and token scope/lifetime and protect client credentials.
Analyze synthetic grant records; no token harvesting.
Steal or Forge Authentication Certificates
Authentication relies on certificate issuance and protected private keys.
Review enrollment approval, templates, issuer trust and key access policy.
Restrict enrollment/signing and support effective certificate revocation.
Inspect a fictional certificate issuance audit; no key theft or fraudulent issuance.
Steal Web Session Technologies
Cookies and session artifacts can act as authentication material.
Review session lifecycle, cookie flags and endpoint protections without cookie contents.
Protect sessions and implement supported expiry/revocation and secure transport.
Verify logout with a synthetic session using normal application behavior; no session theft.
Two-Factor Authentication Evasion
Weak enrollment/recovery and user approval can undermine MFA.
Review factor enrollment, prompt policy and recovery authorization.
Prefer phishing-resistant factors and verified recovery with abuse controls.
Analyze fictional unexpected enrollment/prompt events; no fatigue or interception attempts.
Unsecured Credentials
Secrets may leak into repositories, logs or configuration.
Review existing secret-scan findings and access policy with values redacted.
Move secrets to protected stores and rotate confirmed exposed material.
Locate an explicitly fake marker in an instructor-owned fixture; never validate real secrets.

groups.title: Discovery
groups.goal: Use bounded authorized read-only inventory to understand assets and permissions while protecting personal data and secrets.

commands.title: Windows identity, OS and network inventory
commands.code:
# Run only in the approved host session; protect exported identifiers.
whoami
Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem | Select-Object Caption,Version,BuildNumber
Get-NetIPConfiguration
Get-NetTCPConnection | Select-Object State,LocalAddress,LocalPort,RemoteAddress,RemotePort
Get-Date -Format o
commands.interpretation: A point-in-time view is not exhaustive inventory, remote reachability or proof of compromise. Access failures mean incomplete visibility.

commands.title: Linux host and interface inventory
commands.code:
# Approved host session; no network sweep or file-content search.
id
cat /etc/os-release
uname -r
ip address show
ip route show
ss -lnt
date -u
commands.interpretation: Tools may be absent or restricted. These commands reveal local identity/configuration only; they do not establish that adjacent assets are reachable.

verify: Obtain owner-approved host/resource scope and read privileges. Decide which metadata is needed; avoid browser history, private file contents and secrets.
Record command/API, identity, time, platform and access errors. Reconcile point-in-time output with owner inventory and retained change records.
Classify differences as unexpected, legitimate, stale or unknown. An administrator's view must not be presented as an unauthenticated capability.
fix: Restrict unnecessary enumeration permissions and exposed management interfaces without breaking necessary administration.
Maintain inventories with owners and monitor unexpected read activity using identity and resource context.
retest: Repeat the same approved metadata query and verify expected allowed/denied roles.
Confirm inventory reconciliation and telemetry collection; retain unresolved assets instead of reporting absence.
groups.detection: Discovery commands overlap with legitimate administration. Use principal, host, volume, target scope and change context rather than alerting on a command name alone.
topics: Account Discovery
Account lists expose identities and role relationships.
Review approved account metadata and enumeration permissions.
Limit directory read scope where supported and monitor unusual enumeration.
Classify a synthetic account export; no real user profiling.
Application Window Discovery
Visible windows can reveal active work and sensitive applications.
Review approved endpoint metadata policy; avoid window titles with private content.
Limit unnecessary desktop observation and protect interactive sessions.
Use a fictional window inventory rather than inspect another person's desktop.
Browser Information Discovery
History and bookmarks may reveal private work and identities.
Review browser management configuration without personal browsing records.
Restrict profile access and manage browser policy.
Analyze a synthetic profile-policy export; no browsing-history collection.
Cloud Infrastructure Discovery
Read APIs expose cloud resources and topology.
Review approved resource inventory and reader-role scope across regions.
Use scoped read roles and organization-wide inventory ownership.
Inspect an existing redacted resource export without cloud writes.
Cloud Service Dashboard
Consoles display resources and privileged operational context.
Review assigned console roles and session audit.
Apply least privilege and strong session/device requirements.
Review a fictional read-only dashboard role matrix.
Cloud Service Discovery
SaaS integrations reveal identity and data dependencies.
Review approved SaaS inventory and integration grants.
Manage application consent and ownership and remove unused integrations.
Map a fictional SaaS dependency export.
Container and Resource Discovery
Cluster metadata exposes workloads, permissions and hosting boundaries.
Review approved cluster inventory and API-reader scope without secret objects.
Restrict cluster read grants and protect management access.
Inspect inert workload manifests and a redacted resource list.
Device Driver Discovery

Review owner driver inventory, publisher and supported revision.
Use supported signed drivers and controlled updates.
Compare a provided driver manifest with vendor servicing records.
Domain Trust Discovery

Minimize unnecessary trust and constrain privileged cross-domain access.
Analyze a fictional trust diagram; no cross-domain probing.
File and Directory Discovery

Apply least-privilege storage access and meaningful ownership.
Classify instructor-provided synthetic directory names.
Group Policy Discovery
Policy describes control assignments and administrative trust.
Review a redacted approved policy export and its publishers.
Protect policy management and remove excessive grants.
Identify an excessive permission in a fictional policy export.
Network Share Discovery

Review approved share inventory, effective access and intended clients.
Restrict share rights and separate data from executable deployment paths.
Evaluate a synthetic share/role access matrix without enumerating adjacent systems.
Network Sniffing
Network observation can reveal peers but also private content.
Review sensor placement, permission and metadata-only retention policy.
Restrict capture rights and protect transport and captured evidence.
Map peers from a synthetic flow fixture; no live packet capture.
Peripheral Device Discovery
Peripheral inventories reveal attached trust and data paths.
Review owner device inventory and admission events.
Manage device access and protect sensitive hardware identities.
Compare a fictional peripheral list with an approved baseline.
Permission Groups Discovery

Review effective membership and approved role justification.
Minimize privileged groups and review nested grants.
Inspect a synthetic group graph for unintended privilege.
Process Discovery

Protect sensitive metadata and monitor unusual enumeration context.

Query Registry

Review approved specific keys and access rights without secret-bearing values.
Protect sensitive keys and maintain configuration baselines.
Inspect an instructor-provided non-secret key export.
Remote System Discovery

Compare owner inventory with one approved connection and boundary policy.
Segment systems and manage exposed discovery services.
Check a single approved host/port; no network sweep.
Software Discovery

Reconcile package, artifact and running component identifiers.
Maintain supported versions and authoritative software inventory.
Compare a harmless package export with its running-build record.
System Information Discovery
OS/build/architecture facts anchor applicability decisions.
Record local OS build and vendor servicing evidence.
Patch supported systems and protect unnecessary public disclosure.
Collect the approved host's OS metadata and record limitations.
System Network Configuration Discovery
Local addresses and routes describe a host's configured view.
Review interface, route, DNS and IPv6 configuration.
Remove unnecessary routes/interfaces and manage resolver policy.
Read local interface/route metadata without changing network configuration.
System Network Connections Discovery
Connections reveal current peers and states, not all historic traffic.
Compare local connection metadata with retained network flow evidence.
Restrict unnecessary egress and assign service owners.
Inspect approved local connection metadata; no packet-content capture.
System Owner/User Discovery
Current session identity differs from asset ownership.
Review local identity metadata and owner inventory separately.
Protect sessions and maintain asset ownership records.
Record your supplied test identity and distinguish it from asset owner.
System Service Discovery
Service metadata identifies execution identities and configuration.
Review state, identity, path and owner-approved baseline.
Use least-privilege services and protect configuration writers.
Inspect one approved service without starting or stopping it.
System Time Discovery
Clock alignment affects evidence correlation; time inspection is not inherently malicious.

Maintain trusted time synchronization and note clock offsets.
Compare a synthetic source event and collector time; no timed malicious logic.

Review owner architecture and documented analysis assumptions.
Use independent evidence and avoid overclaiming one environment's coverage.
Compare fictional analysis contexts; do not build sandbox-detection logic.

groups.title: Lateral Movement
groups.goal: Validate internal identity and network boundaries using supplied test principals and inert content, without pivoting or session theft.
verify: Create a source-principal/destination/service matrix with expected allowed and denied paths. Scope every destination explicitly; internal location is not authorization.

Use existing route/access evidence or one normal approved request with supplied identities. Capture source/destination and authentication/application result; a port connection is not successful lateral access.
Correlate both ends and central identity events. For exploitable services, establish CVE applicability separately; do not use stolen sessions, hashes or tickets.
fix: Segment unnecessary peer access, narrow remote administration/deployment rights and patch exposed internal services.
Protect session material and shared executable content; revoke unauthorized grants through incident procedures.
retest: Repeat original matrix cells with fresh synthetic identities and verify required workflows still work.
Confirm denied paths produce expected evidence and response, and document untested destinations.
groups.detection: Join source endpoint, destination authentication, application and network events. A local test event alone does not prove end-to-end lateral detection.
topics: Exploitation of Remote Services
An internal service may expose a remotely reachable flaw.
Check exact build, required access and network exposure using the CVE guide.
Patch and restrict service access to intended peers.
Use version/configuration checks, not an SMB or other remote exploit.
Internal Spear Phishing
A trusted internal sender can still make a deceptive request.
Review fictional message provenance, access request and reporting chain.
Apply internal mail scrutiny and independently verify sensitive requests.
Run a labeled tabletop; do not send deceptive messages to staff.
Lateral Tool Transfer
Transferred files can introduce unreviewed tools to another host.
Review transfer actor, destination, artifact hash and business authorization.
Restrict admin transfers and require trusted artifacts.
Analyze a provided inert transfer record; no attack tool movement.
Remote Service Session Hijacking
An existing session has identity and lifecycle boundaries.
Review session ownership, reconnect events and revocation policy.
Protect sessions and restrict reconnect/session-management rights.
Review fictional reconnect anomalies; no session hijack.
Remote Services
Legitimate remote access can cross internal boundaries.
Review expected roles, MFA/device policy and both-end session evidence.
Use scoped remote administration and segmentation.
Check a supplied test principal against a documented allowed/denied matrix.
Replication Through Removable Media

Review approved device and file-transfer metadata.
Control media admission and execution and track provenance.
Review an inert removable-media event without spreading software.
Software Deployment Tools

Review package approval, operator and target-group changes.
Protect orchestration roles and require scope approval.
Inspect a fictional deployment for unauthorized destination expansion.
Taint Shared Content
