Compare shared artifact hashes, writers and change approvals.
Protect shared templates/executables and separate write from execution trust.
Detect a changed inert file in an instructor manifest; no infectious content.
Use Alternate Authentication Material
Hashes, tickets and tokens may provide access outside password flows.
Review authentication method and grant/session metadata without values.
Protect privileged sessions and limit legacy authentication where supported.
Analyze synthetic sign-in method records; no pass-the-hash or ticket replay.

groups.title: Collection
groups.goal: Assess data access and collection controls with inert instructor-owned data, never private conversations, credentials or real employee content.

commands.title: Inspect explicitly approved inert fixture metadata
commands.code:
# Replace with a directory containing instructor-owned non-sensitive fixtures only.
Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath 'C:\ApprovedAssessment\Fixtures' -File | Select-Object Name,Length,LastWriteTimeUtc
commands.interpretation: This is a bounded metadata listing, not recursive collection or proof of data access outside the fixture directory. Do not point it at real user profiles or sensitive repositories.

verify: Assign owners and sensitivity classes to data stores and map roles to expected reads/exports. Use only instructor-created non-sensitive fixtures.
Review access, export, staging and capture permissions; compare one approved fixture access event with expected audit fields.
Use policy review or a supplied synthetic denied-access case for unauthorized paths. Do not capture audio/video, mailbox contents or keyboard input.
fix: Reduce excessive read/export rights and enforce supported data classification and access controls.
Protect export/staging locations and restrict unattended collection and capture features.
retest: Repeat fixture access with the same roles and verify allow/deny and audit outcomes.
Confirm legitimate collaboration works and no sensitive content appears in training evidence.
groups.detection: Correlate object access, export operations and new staging artifacts with principal and business purpose. Routine reads are not necessarily malicious collection.
topics: Archive Collected Data
Archiving consolidates data but is also a normal business action.
Review approved export/archive events and input classification.
Restrict sensitive exports and protect archive destinations.
Inspect an inert archive manifest, not an archive of real corporate data.
Audio Capture
Microphone use can disclose private conversations.
Review app microphone permission and approved device policy.
Restrict capture to authorized applications and consented purposes.
Analyze a synthetic microphone permission event; no recording.
Automated Collection
Automation can amplify excessive read privileges.
Review job role, approved data scope and read/export audit.
Limit service-account data access and export rates as appropriate.
Review a harmless synthetic collection-job manifest without scraping real files.
Data from Cloud Storage Object
Object access depends on identity and storage policy.
Review bucket/container/object policy and access audit metadata.
Use least privilege, private storage and controlled export destinations.
Inspect an instructor-provided redacted storage access log.
Data from Information Repositories
Collaboration systems hold broad searchable business context.
Review workspace/repository grants and export audit.
Limit external sharing and unnecessary bulk-export rights.
Evaluate a synthetic collaboration access matrix.
Data from Local System
Local files may be readable beyond intended roles.
Review effective permissions and owner-approved fixture access.
Apply least privilege and endpoint data protection.
List only the approved inert fixture directory's metadata.
Data from Network Shared Drive
Share and filesystem permissions both matter.
Review effective share/file access and object-read audit.
Narrow grants and protect sensitive shares and export paths.
Assess a synthetic role/share/file access matrix.
Data Staged
A staging area concentrates collected material before transfer.
Review new archive/staging metadata, writers and approved purpose.
Control staging/export permissions and monitor sensitive data movement.
Identify an unexpected inert staging entry in a manifest.
Email Collection
Mail export/delegation can expose broad private content.
Review mailbox grants, export policy and audit metadata, not message bodies.
Restrict delegation and bulk export and protect identity sessions.
Analyze a fictional mailbox-export event without mailbox access.
Input Capture
Input capture risks disclosure before application protections apply.
Review endpoint capture permissions and unexpected tool alerts.
Restrict untrusted software and protect input/authentication UI.
Use a synthetic capture alert; no keylogger.
Screen Capture
Screen images can contain sensitive information outside file controls.
Review approved application capture rights and device policy.
Limit capture/sharing and protect interactive sessions.
Use a fictional screenshot-permission record; no user screen capture.
Video Capture
Camera access requires explicit consent and policy.
Review camera permissions and authorized usage records.
Restrict unauthorized applications and provide clear consent controls.
Analyze a synthetic camera-permission event; no recording.

groups.title: Command and Control
groups.goal: Evaluate outbound communication policy and telemetry using ordinary requests or synthetic traces, not malware channels, covert signaling or tunneling.

commands.title: Observe one ordinary approved HTTPS request
commands.code:
# Replace with an instructor-owned approved HTTPS endpoint returning static text.
curl --head --connect-timeout 5 --max-time 10 https://lab.example/
commands.interpretation: This validates an ordinary request and related telemetry only. It is not C2, carries no commands or data payload and cannot establish coverage of covert/encrypted variants.

verify: Document approved destination/service owners, egress policy, proxies, DNS and remote-access software. Do not contact suspicious destinations.
Perform one ordinary request to an instructor-owned endpoint or review supplied synthetic flow metadata; capture source, process/identity where available, destination, time and policy outcome.
Compare source evidence with network/endpoint collection, intended alert and response. Encrypted application contents may be unavailable; record metadata visibility and privacy constraints.
fix: Restrict unnecessary egress and remote-access tools and require destination ownership and reviewed proxy/DNS policy.
Collect useful endpoint/network context and repair coverage across fallback routes and regions without weakening TLS validation.
retest: Repeat the same ordinary request or query fixture and verify policy and telemetry outcomes.
Confirm required business traffic still works and distinguish synthetic replay from live communication detection.
groups.detection: Correlate connection/process identity, DNS, destination ownership and timing. Common protocols, encryption and unusual ports are clues, not automatic proof of malware or guaranteed detection bypass.
topics: Application Layer Protocol
Ordinary application protocols may carry unauthorized communications.
Review destination, process, identity and permitted business use.
Use explicit egress policy and application/endpoint context.
Make one approved static HTTPS request; no remote commands.
Communication Through Removable Media
Media can carry information across an air gap.
Review media admission, transfer approval and chain-of-custody records.
Control media use and maintain approved transfer processes.
Review a fictional media-transfer manifest; no command exchange.
Data Obfuscation
Representations may obscure content, but encoding is not inherently malicious.
Review provenance and available behavioral context without processing unknown payloads.
Use layered endpoint/network controls and safe artifact handling.
Classify a harmless text fixture, not hidden command traffic.
Dynamic Resolution
Changing destination resolution can complicate static policy.
Review synthetic DNS history, ownership and actual resolved endpoints.
Use monitored resolvers and destination-aware egress policy.
Analyze a fictional changing-DNS trace; no DGA or fast-flux setup.
Encrypted Channel
Encryption protects content and limits network content visibility.
Review approved TLS metadata and endpoint process identity.
Use destination and endpoint controls while preserving legitimate encryption.
Observe ordinary approved HTTPS metadata; no encrypted command channel.
Fallback Channels
Alternate paths can remain available after a primary path is blocked.
Review approved topology and policy coverage across interfaces/providers.
Apply consistent egress and monitoring across approved routes.
Analyze a synthetic primary/alternate path matrix; no bypass channel.
Inversion of Control
Internal infrastructure may mediate externally initiated workflows.
Review actor/request chains and trusted integration callbacks.
Authenticate integrations and constrain callback privileges.
Trace a fictional approved callback event; no relay setup.
Multi-Stage Channels
Several relays can separate origin from endpoint visibility.
Correlate approved proxy/request IDs and flow metadata with known ownership.
Restrict unapproved relays and retain trusted proxy audit.
Analyze a synthetic multi-hop diagram without configuring relays.
Non-Application Layer Protocol
Lower-layer traffic may fall outside application monitoring.
Review allowed protocols and sensor metadata coverage.
Restrict unnecessary protocols and retain boundary flow evidence.
Classify a supplied synthetic ICMP/TCP flow fixture; no raw channel.
Non-Standard Port
A port number does not reliably identify protocol or intent.
Compare protocol metadata with explicit destination/service policy.
Use application-aware controls and restrict unexplained services.
Review a synthetic protocol/port mismatch; no firewall bypass attempt.
Protocol Tunneling
A permitted protocol can encapsulate another flow.
Review approved tunnel inventory and endpoint/network context.
Restrict unauthorized tunnels and protect legitimate gateway administration.
Analyze prerecorded synthetic tunnel metadata; no tunnel construction.
Proxy
Intermediaries can obscure origin but also support normal access.
Review approved proxy ownership, actor and request chain.
Constrain proxy configuration and retain necessary request audit.
Inspect a fictional proxy chain; no anonymous relay configuration.
Remote Access Software
Legitimate remote support tools can provide broad control.
Review installed tool ownership, unattended access and session audit.
Allowlist necessary tools and require approved sessions and strong authentication.
Review an approved session record; no covert remote-control installation.
Traffic Duplication
Mirrored traffic creates another sensitive collection path.
Review switch/cloud mirroring configuration, destination and authorization.
Restrict mirror administration and protect collector access and retention.
Evaluate a redacted mirror-policy export; no traffic interception.
Web Service
Public services may host unauthorized communication content.
Review endpoint/process destination context without visiting suspicious posts.
Constrain unnecessary service access and monitor approved integrations.
Analyze a fictional public-service connection event; no command posting.

groups.title: Exfiltration
groups.goal: Validate data-loss policy and egress evidence with synthetic metadata or a small explicitly approved inert transfer, never real sensitive data or stealth channels.
verify: Name source classification, approved destination, identity and expected data-loss policy. Choose instructor-owned inert text or synthetic transfer records only.
Prefer an offline policy/query fixture. If the owner separately approves an actual transfer, fix the destination, small size and ordinary supported protocol; do not split, hide or tunnel data.
Record source/destination audit, policy decision, alert/ticket and confirmed denial/containment. Do not equate a dashboard alert with prevention of transfer.
fix: Restrict excessive export/sharing and unapproved destinations; enforce supported classification and data-loss controls.
Repair policy and telemetry gaps across cloud, endpoint and physical transfer paths with accountable owners.
retest: Repeat the same inert policy fixture or separately approved transfer and verify actual allow/deny outcome plus expected alert.
Confirm authorized sharing works and document blind spots and privacy limits.
groups.detection: Join file/object access and export/egress evidence with identity, classification and destination. Small or scheduled transfers are not guaranteed to evade controls; test timing with synthetic logs rather than operational stealth.
topics: Automated Exfiltration
Automation can move data without repeated interactive approval.
Review export-job identity, source classification and destination policy.
Restrict automated export grants and destinations.
Analyze a synthetic export-job event; no sensitive data transfer.
Data Transfer Size Limits
Volume-only detections can miss aggregate behavior across events.
Review synthetic cumulative transfer totals against classification and destination policy.
Use identity/classification context and appropriate aggregation rather than volume alone.
Test a query on provided small-transfer records; no chunking/evasion implementation.
Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol
Unexpected protocols can expose egress policy gaps.
Review permitted protocol inventory and policy coverage.
Restrict unnecessary protocols and monitor approved exceptions.
Classify synthetic alternate-protocol events; no covert transport.
Exfiltration Over Cloud Service
External storage sharing can cross organization data boundaries.
Review storage ownership, sharing grants and export audit.
Restrict unapproved tenants/accounts and apply data-sharing policy.
Evaluate a fictional organization-versus-personal storage policy case.
Exfiltration Over Command and Control Channel
A communication path may also carry collected data.
Correlate provided export and connection metadata by identity and time.
Constrain unauthorized egress and protect source-data access.
Analyze a synthetic correlation fixture; no C2 or data payload.
Exfiltration Over Other Network Medium
Secondary radio/network interfaces may bypass the intended managed path.
Review approved interface inventory and device policy.
Manage unauthorized interfaces and enforce consistent endpoint data policy.
Review a fictional interface/egress matrix; no alternate wireless transfer.
Exfiltration Over Physical Medium
Physical media can move data beyond network controls.
Review device, export approval and custody records.
Control removable-media access and authorized data handling.
Run a fictional media-loss tabletop; no copying sensitive files.
Exfiltration Over Web Service
External sharing endpoints create data-release boundaries.
Review approved upload/share destinations and source classification.
Restrict unapproved sharing and enforce supported data-loss controls.
Evaluate a synthetic upload policy fixture; no paste-site transfer.
Scheduled Transfer
Time-based automation may move data outside attended hours.
Review approved job schedule, identity and consistent policy coverage.
Apply data policy continuously and alert on unapproved export schedules.
Test a query on synthetic timestamps; no off-hours stealth transfer.

groups.title: Impact
groups.goal: Assess resilience, permissions and response to damaging outcomes through read-only checks and tabletops, not destruction, ransomware, flooding or firmware changes.

commands.title: Read approved service availability metadata
commands.code:
# Authorized host, read-only. Does not stop or restart anything.
Get-Service | Select-Object Name,Status,StartType
commands.interpretation: Service state is a point-in-time availability clue, not proof of root cause or recovery readiness. Recovery arrangements remain with the team's existing procedures.

verify: Identify critical services/data, authorized operators, dependency owners and approved incident contacts. Use existing recovery evidence rather than adding snapshot/reset procedures.

Review destructive-action permissions, independent availability telemetry and owner-provided recovery exercise records. No deletion, encryption, disk/firmware write, flooding or production control changes.

Run a hypothetical incident with synthetic events: identify impact, authorize containment, notify owners and demonstrate decisions. Mark tabletop results separately from executed recovery or live detection.
fix: Restrict destructive management actions, separate critical administration and preserve independent incident evidence.
Maintain supported systems, resource limits and owner-tested recovery/service continuity procedures; protect those procedures from unauthorized changes.
retest: Repeat the failed permission or tabletop decision check and confirm responsible staff can follow it.
Review evidence from existing owner-run continuity exercises; do not claim recovery was tested when only a tabletop was performed.
groups.detection: Correlate destructive API/change requests, integrity changes, resource saturation and service loss with independent telemetry. An outage is not automatically malicious, and an alert does not demonstrate recovery.
topics: Account Destruction
Deleted identities or tenants can remove operational access.
Review deletion permissions, approval and owner-provided recovery evidence.
Separate destructive privileges and protect break-glass access.
Run a fictional account-deletion incident; do not delete accounts.
Data Destruction
Deletion or corruption can cause irreversible business loss.
Review write/delete grants, integrity telemetry and continuity records.
Limit destructive rights and protect independent recovery arrangements.
Review a synthetic deletion event and response ownership; no file destruction.
Data Encrypted for Impact
Unauthorized encryption can deny access to business data.
Review rapid-change alerts, write authority and owner resilience evidence.
Constrain write privileges and protect supported endpoint and recovery controls.
Analyze synthetic ransomware-like event metadata; no encryptor.
Data Manipulation
Unauthorized changes can harm integrity without obvious outage.
Review change audit, approval and independently reconciled business records.
Use separation of duties and integrity validation for critical data.
Find a changed value in instructor-provided fictional records.
Defacement
Unauthorized published content indicates an integrity failure.
Compare deployment/content audit and approved site artifacts.
Protect publishing rights and reviewed deployment workflows.
Identify a change in inert before/after page fixtures, not a real site.
Disk Wipe
Low-level storage writes can make data and systems unavailable.
Review raw disk/destructive permissions and independent storage alerts.
Restrict destructive device access and protect continuity procedures.
Run a fictional disk-loss tabletop; no format or raw writes.
Endpoint Denial of Service
Resource exhaustion or faults can impair a host.
Review resource limits, health telemetry and root-cause evidence.
Patch faults and enforce supported workload/resource controls.
Analyze prerecorded synthetic saturation metrics; no crash or stress attack.
Firmware Corruption
Broken firmware can impair devices and physical operations.
Review update authorization, vendor integrity and maintenance ownership.
Protect firmware administration and use supported signed updates.
Conduct an owner-led device-loss tabletop; no firmware writes.
Inhibit System Recovery
Tampering with recovery arrangements can worsen an incident.
Review recovery-management permissions and independent change alerts.
Separate recovery administration and protect owner-managed recovery assets.
Review synthetic unauthorized recovery-policy events; no deletion of restore data.
Network Denial of Service
Traffic or device overload can disrupt connectivity.
Review capacity, edge protection and provider escalation evidence.
Use supported rate/resource controls and upstream response arrangements.
Analyze synthetic traffic metrics and escalation decisions; no flooding.
Resource Hijacking
Unapproved workloads can consume compute and budget.
Review workload ownership, usage anomalies and creation/billing audit.
Apply workload admission, least privilege and budget/resource controls.
Identify unexplained usage in a fictional workload report; no miner.
Service Stop
Stopping a dependency can interrupt many workflows.
Review service-management rights and dependency/availability records.
Restrict stop privileges and monitor service state independently.
Inspect approved service metadata and a synthetic stop event; do not stop services.
System Shutdown/Reboot
Unapproved power operations can affect availability and safety.
Review power-management roles, change audit and operational dependencies.
Restrict shutdown rights and coordinate approved maintenance.
Run a fictional shutdown-response tabletop; no reboot commands.
